[Listing Detail] Publish Google (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN publishes tours to Google (Street View / Business Profile); projects track googleUploaded (see docs/analyze.md §2.7 and §3.3). Uses the GoThru/Google integration.

Goal

Implement "Publish Google" in Listing Detail: publish the listed tour to Google, updating the publish state (googleUploaded) and surfacing the result.

Scope

  • Publish-to-Google action for the current listing/tour.
  • Trigger the GoThru-side Google publish flow; show progress and outcome.
  • Update local googleUploaded/publish status on success; handle Google auth/permission requirements.

Out of Scope

  • Update tour / activate-deactivate / reload / discard (separate tasks).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Publish-to-Google action triggers the publish flow and reports progress.
  • On success, the listing reflects a published-to-Google state (googleUploaded).
  • Auth/permission and API errors are surfaced clearly with retry.
  • Requires connectivity; works with the signed-in session.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Publish to Google (happy path)

  1. Open a listing eligible to publish → Publish Google.
  2. Expected: Publish completes; listing shows published-to-Google state.

TC-2 — Already published

  1. Publish a listing that is already on Google.
  2. Expected: Handled gracefully (informs already published / re-publish behavior defined).

TC-3 — Missing Google auth/permission

  1. Attempt publish without required Google authorization.
  2. Expected: Clear prompt/guidance; no crash.

TC-4 — Offline / API error

  1. Attempt publish offline or with a server error.
  2. Expected: Clear error; retry possible; state not corrupted.

TC-5 — Status persistence

  1. Publish, relaunch, reopen.
  2. Expected: Published-to-Google state persists/refetches.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Labels/status/errors translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: GoThru listing state remains consistent with Google publish state.

QA Final Summary — 5 August 2026

Result: PASS

[Listing Detail] Virtual Tour Activate & Deactivate (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: Projects carry virtual_tour_status (see docs/analyze.md §3.3); listing detail lets the user toggle a tour's live/active state via the GoThru API (§2.6/§3.4).

Goal

Implement Activate / Deactivate of a virtual tour in Listing Detail: toggle the tour's live status (virtual_tour_status) on GoThru, with clear current-state display.

Scope

  • A toggle/action to activate or deactivate the virtual tour.
  • Call the GoThru API to set status; update local virtual_tour_status and UI.
  • Confirmation for deactivation (since it affects public visibility); progress + result feedback.

Out of Scope

  • Publish Google / update tour / reload / discard (separate tasks).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Current active/inactive state is clearly shown.
  • Activate sets the tour live; Deactivate takes it offline (virtual_tour_status updated).
  • Deactivation asks for confirmation.
  • API errors surfaced with retry; state stays consistent after restart.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Activate (happy path)

  1. Open an inactive listing → Activate.
  2. Expected: Tour becomes active; status reflects active.

TC-2 — Deactivate with confirmation

  1. On an active listing → Deactivate → confirm.
  2. Expected: Tour becomes inactive; status reflects inactive.

TC-3 — Cancel deactivation

  1. Tap Deactivate, then cancel.
  2. Expected: Tour stays active; no change.

TC-4 — Offline / API error

  1. Toggle while offline or simulate error.
  2. Expected: Clear error; state not changed locally without server confirmation.

TC-5 — State persistence

  1. Toggle, relaunch, reopen.
  2. Expected: The new status persists/refetches correctly.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: State labels/confirmation translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: toggling status does not alter tour content (panoramas/connections).

QA Final Summary — 5 August 2026

Result: PASS

Manual validation was completed on a real mobile device using real data. Activate and Deactivate worked correctly, and no coding bug was found.

[Listing Detail] Reload Images (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: Listing detail can refresh the tour's panorama images from GoThru so the local view matches the server (see docs/analyze.md §2.6, §3.3 panoramas, §3.4 listings API).

Goal

Implement "Reload Images" in Listing Detail: re-fetch the listing's panorama images/thumbnails from the server and refresh the displayed assets (bypassing stale cache).

Scope

  • Reload action that re-fetches panorama images/thumbnails for the listing.
  • Invalidate/refresh cached images so updated server images appear.
  • Progress + result feedback; loading placeholders during reload.

Out of Scope

  • Editing/uploading images; update tour / publish / activate / discard (separate tasks).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Reload re-fetches the listing's panorama images from the server.
  • Stale/cached images are replaced by the latest server versions.
  • Progress shown; errors surfaced with retry.
  • Requires connectivity; UI remains responsive during reload.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Reload images (happy path)

  1. Open a listing → Reload Images.
  2. Expected: Images re-fetch and refresh; progress shown.

TC-2 — Updated server image reflected

  1. Change an image server-side, then Reload.
  2. Expected: The new image appears (no stale cached version).

TC-3 — Offline

  1. Reload while offline.
  2. Expected: Clear "no internet" message; existing images remain.

TC-4 — API error + retry

  1. Simulate a fetch failure, then retry.
  2. Expected: Error surfaced; retry succeeds.

TC-5 — Large listing

  1. Reload a listing with many images.
  2. Expected: Loads with placeholders; UI not frozen.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Reload status/errors translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: reload does not duplicate panoramas or change listing metadata.

QA Final Summary — 5 August 2026

Result: PASS

ListingDetailReloadImages54.mp4

Manual validation was completed by the tester on a real mobile device using real data. Images were successfully reloaded from GoThru; no coding bug was found.

Behavior clarification

After a full-image reload from Level 2, the view returned to Level 1. This is accepted default behavior: Reload Images synchronizes the complete tour, not one level only, and opens the default first level after the full refresh. It is not a coding bug.

[Listing Detail] Discard Changes (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: Listing detail lets the user abandon unsaved local edits and revert to the last saved/server state (see docs/analyze.md §2.6, §3.3 projects/panoramas).

Goal

Implement "Discard Changes" in Listing Detail: revert any unsaved local edits to the listing back to the last saved/server state, with confirmation.

Scope

  • Discard action (with confirm) that drops pending local edits to the listing.
  • Restore fields/assets to the last saved/server values.
  • Reflect the reverted state in the UI immediately.

Out of Scope

  • Saving/updating (separate task); deleting the listing/tour.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Discard prompts for confirmation before reverting.
  • On confirm, unsaved edits are dropped and the last saved/server state is restored.
  • Cancel keeps the in-progress edits.
  • UI reflects the reverted state immediately; no partial/garbled state.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Discard edits (happy path)

  1. Open a listing → make edits → Discard Changes → confirm.
  2. Expected: Edits removed; listing shows the last saved/server values.

TC-2 — Cancel discard

  1. Make edits → Discard → cancel.
  2. Expected: Edits are kept; nothing reverted.

TC-3 — No edits

  1. Tap Discard with no pending changes.
  2. Expected: Graceful no-op / informs nothing to discard.

TC-4 — Discard then re-edit

  1. Discard, then make new edits.
  2. Expected: Editing works normally after a discard.

TC-5 — Navigation guard (if applicable)

  1. Try to leave the screen with unsaved edits.
  2. Expected: Prompt to discard/keep, per the defined behavior.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Confirmation/labels translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: discard reverts only the current listing's unsaved edits — no server data is changed.

QA Summary — 5 August 2026

QA status: Needs developer confirmation

Manual validation was completed on a real mobile device using real data. The expected Discard Changes popup did not appear after the tested edits. This is recorded as a QA note pending developer confirmation; it is not yet classified as a coding bug.

Result and scope clarification

The current Listing Detail behavior saves supported edits directly to GoThru/web:

  • Adding a level is integrated with GoThru and saves immediately.
  • Moving a panorama to another level is integrated with GoThru and saves immediately.
  • Connection editing could not be used as a pending-local-change scenario during this validation.

Therefore, there is no available user action that leaves an unsaved local edit and triggers the Discard Changes confirmation. The absence of the dialog in this flow is expected because the validated changes have already been saved to GoThru. This may be an intended scope/behavior difference from the original issue description. Developer confirmation is required before classifying it as a coding bug.

[Tour Detail] Integrate Auto Label (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN project flag useAutoLabel (added to the projects table in src/pages/init.js); see docs/analyze.md §3.3. Auto Label automatically generates labels/names for panoramas (e.g. sequential or position-based) instead of manual naming.

Goal

Implement "Auto Label" in Tour Detail: automatically generate labels/names for the project's panoramas, controlled by the project's useAutoLabel setting, so users don't have to name each panorama manually.

Scope

  • Toggle/trigger Auto Label for a project (persist useAutoLabel).
  • Generate labels for panoramas (e.g. sequential / order- or position-based) and apply them.
  • Show the applied labels in the panorama list; result remains manually editable.
  • Re-apply consistently when panoramas are added (per the agreed rule).

Out of Scope

  • Auto Level (separate task); manual rename of individual panoramas (existing behavior).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Auto Label generates and applies labels to the project's panoramas.
  • The useAutoLabel setting persists on the project.
  • Labels are visible in the panorama list and remain manually editable.
  • Labeling is consistent/ordered; no duplicate/empty labels.
  • Works offline (local operation); survives restart.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Enable Auto Label (happy path)

  1. Open a tour → enable/run Auto Label.
  2. Expected: Panoramas receive generated labels; useAutoLabel is on.

TC-2 — Labels shown in list

  1. View the panorama list after labeling.
  2. Expected: Each panorama shows its auto-generated label.

TC-3 — Ordering/consistency

  1. Inspect labels across the tour.
  2. Expected: Labels follow the defined order rule; no duplicates/empties.

TC-4 — Manual override

  1. Manually rename an auto-labeled panorama.
  2. Expected: Manual label is kept (per the agreed override rule).

TC-5 — Add panorama after auto-label

  1. With Auto Label on, add a new panorama.
  2. Expected: It receives a label consistent with the scheme.

TC-6 — Persistence after restart

  1. Auto-label, relaunch, reopen.
  2. Expected: Labels and useAutoLabel setting persist.

Regression watch: auto-labeling changes only labels — not images, levels, or connections.
